items.body:
<details open>

ggml-openvino: expand model support, optimize NPU,GPU and memory usage (#32172)

* ggml-openvino: fix SWA mask detection

When the SWA cache size matches the full cache size, identify SWA
layers by the number of layers using each mask instead of cache size;
the larger group is SWA, and a tie leaves the layers unclassified.

* ggml-openvino: fix SWA KV cache write indices

Give SWA KV cache index tensors unique input names (a _swa suffix, like
the masks) to prevent them from being merged with the full-attention
cache indices.

* ggml-openvino: classify SWA layers only when the mask shows the window

Two attention masks do not imply SWA: DeepSeek sparse attention uses two
full-attention masks with the same name. When cache extents match,
classify the larger mask group as SWA only once its mask has fewer keys
per row than the other mask. Keep the classification per KV cache buffer
so new sequences reuse the same graph, and include swa_layers when
checking graph reuse.

* ggml-openvino: classify SWA layers from the first graph

Waiting for the window to appear in the mask caused a mid-sequence graph
recompile (~9 s for Gemma-4 at -c 1024 after position 512).

SWA classification already gives each mask group its own mask, KV write
indices, and attention size, which is correct whether or not the mask is
a sliding window. Stateful mask rebuild recovers the window from the
mask, or the causal mask for full attention. Classify the larger of two
mask groups from the first graph and drop the per-KV-buffer bookkeeping.

* ggml-openvino: mark SWA fallback as a model-level heuristic

items.body:
<details open>

cuda: decode the conv2d patch indices with fastdiv (#32492)

The implicit GEMM conv2d kernel recovers the channel and the kernel
position of each reduction index with three integer divisions by
runtime divisors, once per loaded row of every tile. Outside the 3x3
and 1x1 specializations this integer division bounds the kernel:
removing it halves the time on long reductions.

Divide with the precomputed magic numbers of fastdiv instead. The 3x3
and 1x1 specializations keep their compile time divisors.

test-backend-ops -o CONV_2D: 2006/2006 on CUDA0.

CONV_2D, F16 kernel, us/run on an RTX PRO 6000:
  [2054,1,768] k [7,1,768,768]       221 -> 138
  [16390,1,384] k [7,1,384,384]      433 -> 266
  [65542,1,192] k [7,1,192,192]      420 -> 271
  [8240,1,256] k [11,1,256,256]      165 -> 108
  [19,19,256,16] k [4,4,256,4096]   1672 -> 1076

</details>
